paper.title_en: Light induced magnetization in d-wave superconductors
paper.abstract_en: We develop a microscopic theory of the inverse Faraday effect in weakly disordered $s$- and $d$-wave superconductors. The Keldysh--Nambu quasiclassical formalism is extended to retain the particle-hole asymmetric terms, and the dc current induced by monochromatic radiation is computed to second order in the field and to first order in the wave vector, with elastic impurity scattering treated in the Born approximation. At finite wave vector the radiation induces an oscillation of the order parameter amplitude -- the Schmid--Higgs amplitude mode -- that is linear in the field. It is driven by the component of the electric field along the photon wave vector and appears for both $s$- and $d$-wave pairing. The amplitude mode contribution to the static magnetization sets in at $ω=2Δ$ and diverges as $(ω-2Δ)^{-1}$ for an isotropic gap, whereas for $d$-wave pairing it is finite at all frequencies and changes sign near $ω\approx 2\sqrt{2}Δ$. This contribution is of the first order in the particle-hole asymmetry, and it is not enhanced by the disorder scattering rate. The orbital magnetization that exists already in the normal state and the contribution of the charge imbalance are not evaluated.
